propositions: DC backend lacks value-level pinning coverage: test_backend_contract.py only asserts shape (dict keys present) not values, leaving recent DC implementations unvalidated against production-hardened Cloud baselines

The shared map_fields_to_remote in jira_family/outbound_mapper.py is never exercised through WikiTextCodec, creating a blind spot where regressions in DC composition (truncation, non-str guards, status/priority mapping) would reach users uncaught

DC's probe classification cannot be tested through the _backend() fixture because FakeTransport.probe_remote() returns a static stub result, making it impossible to pin all four branches (PRESENT_RESOLVED, PRESENT_FILTERED, ARCHIVED_OR_MOVED, UNREACHABLE)

DC and Cloud share identical DEFAULT_RESOLVED_STATUSES values by coincidence, making any pin written at defaults vacuous and unable to detect whether DC actually binds its own config versus Cloud's hardcoded set

Cloud and DC legitimately diverge in output format (ADF vs wiki markup, accountId vs name) and codec behavior (rich text normalization is identity in wiki but transforms in ADF), requiring parametrized expectations rather than shared assertions
